# SYN-001 — Derivation of the synthetic three-component ideal fixture

**Package:** P01 (Fable lead, Opus second)  
**Author:** Fable 5.1, 2026-09-06  
**Authority:** plan v1.1 §3 (definitions, sanity values, flowsheet, variants, tolerances); blueprint v3.1 §4.2, §6.2, §8.1 (A09)  
**State/units/zero-flow semantics:** ADR 0001  
**Machine-readable values:** `benchmarks/syn001/reference_values.yaml` (20 significant digits, generated by Fable from the definitions in §1 with mpmath at 40 digits; independent of the oracle code)  
**Status:** derivation numerically verified by Fable; process-modeling review pending (human)

SYN-001 is explicitly synthetic. A, B, C are artificial pseudo-components with molecular weight 0.100 kg/mol, no chemical identity, and no elemental formula; elemental verification is `NOT_APPLICABLE`. Nothing in this document is an experimental or real-chemistry claim. Its purpose is to isolate numerical behavior from real-data selection (plan §3.1).

## 1. Definitions (verbatim from plan §3.1)

Constants:

| Parameter | A | B | C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reference boiling temperature T_b,i, K | 320 | 360 | 400 |
| Vapor reference enthalpy offset L_i, J/mol | 25 000 | 30 000 | 35 000 |
| Heat capacity c_p (both phases), J/(mol K) | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| Liquid molar volume v_i, m³/mol | 1.0e-4 | 1.0e-4 | 1.0e-4 |
| Molecular weight M_i, kg/mol | 0.100 | 0.100 | 0.100 |

T_r = 300 K, P_r = 100 000 Pa, R = 8.31446261815324 J/(mol K). Declared test domain: 280 K ≤ T ≤ 440 K, 50 000 Pa ≤ P ≤ 200 000 Pa. No critical-region or extra-phase claim is made; outside the domain the provider returns a typed domain failure.

Pure-component molar Gibbs energies:

    a(T)     = c_p [ (T − T_r) − T ln(T/T_r) ]
    g_i^L    = a(T) + v_i (P − P_r)
    g_i^V    = a(T) + L_i − T L_i / T_b,i + R T ln(P/P_r)

Mixtures are ideal in both phases: μ_i^L = g_i^L + RT ln x_i and μ_i^V = g_i^V + RT ln y_i.

## 2. Enthalpies from the potentials (h = g − T ∂g/∂T)

Differentiate a(T): ∂a/∂T = c_p [1 − ln(T/T_r) − T·(1/T)] = −c_p ln(T/T_r). Therefore

    a − T ∂a/∂T = c_p [(T − T_r) − T ln(T/T_r)] + c_p T ln(T/T_r) = c_p (T − T_r).

Liquid: ∂g_i^L/∂T = ∂a/∂T (the v_i (P − P_r) term is T-independent), so

    h_i^L = g_i^L − T ∂g_i^L/∂T = c_p (T − T_r) + v_i (P − P_r).

Vapor: ∂g_i^V/∂T = ∂a/∂T − L_i/T_b,i + R ln(P/P_r), so

    h_i^V = c_p (T − T_r) + L_i − T L_i/T_b,i + RT ln(P/P_r) + T L_i/T_b,i − RT ln(P/P_r) = c_p (T − T_r) + L_i.

Both agree with plan §3.1. Consequences worth recording:

- Entropies s = −∂g/∂T: s_i^L = c_p ln(T/T_r); s_i^V = c_p ln(T/T_r) + L_i/T_b,i − R ln(P/P_r).
- Volumes ∂g/∂P: liquid v_i (incompressible), vapor RT/P (ideal gas), as intended.
- Heat capacity ∂h/∂T = c_p in both phases, so the enthalpy of vaporization at P_r, h_i^V − h_i^L = L_i, is temperature-independent; at other pressures it is L_i − v_i (P − P_r).
- At (T_b,i, P_r): g_i^V − g_i^L = L_i − L_i = 0. T_b,i is therefore exactly the pure-component boiling temperature at P_r, and the vaporization entropy there is L_i/T_b,i, consistent with Δg = Δh − TΔs = 0.
- Mixture enthalpy: with g_mix = Σ x_i (g_i + RT ln x_i), the term T ∂(RT ln x_i)/∂T = RT ln x_i cancels in g − T g_T, so h_mix = Σ x_i h_i (no excess enthalpy). A stream's enthalpy flow is Ḣ = Σ n_i h_i^phase(T, P), linear in component flows.

Numerical check (Fable, mpmath, 40 digits): max |h − (g − T ∂g/∂T)| over T ∈ {280, 300, 347, 360, 440} K, P ∈ {5e4, 1e5, 2e5} Pa, both phases, all components: 7.5e-37 J/mol (differentiation-noise level).

## 3. K-values from phase equilibrium

Equal chemical potentials, μ_i^L = μ_i^V, give RT ln(y_i/x_i) = g_i^L − g_i^V, i.e.

    K_i ≡ y_i/x_i = exp[(g_i^L − g_i^V)/(RT)],
    g_i^L − g_i^V = v_i (P − P_r) − L_i + T L_i/T_b,i − RT ln(P/P_r).

Dividing by RT and rearranging:

    K_i(T, P) = (P_r/P) exp[ (L_i/R)(1/T_b,i − 1/T) + v_i (P − P_r)/(RT) ].

This is the plan §3.1 expression. K_i is composition-independent (ideal mixing), the term v_i (P − P_r)/(RT) is the Poynting-type liquid correction and vanishes at P_r, and K_i(T_b,i, P_r) = 1 exactly. Because the ideal-mixing terms appear only through the difference RT ln y_i − RT ln x_i, the working form y_i = K_i x_i never evaluates ln 0 for an absent component; this is the guard required by plan §3.1 and ADR 0001 D3.3.

Numerical check: max relative difference between the closed form and exp[(g^L − g^V)/(RT)] over the domain grid is 3.2e-40.

Derivatives needed later (P02/K01 callback tests):

    ∂ ln K_i/∂T = [L_i − v_i (P − P_r)] / (R T²),    ∂ ln K_i/∂P = −1/P + v_i/(RT).

At 360 K, P_r: ∂ln K/∂T = (0.0232006858, 0.0278408229, 0.0324809601) K⁻¹; ∂ln K/∂P = −9.96659101e-6 Pa⁻¹ for all three.

## 4. Reference flowsheet and its equations

Streams (all at P_r; all pressure drops zero): S1 fresh feed (fixed: n = (1, 1, 1) mol/s, 300 K, liquid); S2 mixer outlet; S3 heater outlet (350 K); S4 flash vapor product (T_f); S5 flash liquid (T_f); S6 recycle = r·S5; S7 purge = (1 − r)·S5. Nominal T_f = 360 K, r = 0.5.

Unit equations (ADR 0001 sign convention: duties positive into the unit):

- Mixer (adiabatic): n_S2 = n_S1 + n_S6; Ḣ(S2) = Ḣ(S1) + Ḣ(S6); P_S2 = P_S1 = P_S6. In v0.0 the enthalpy closure is a bracketed scalar solve for T_S2 restricted to the subcooled-liquid domain, with a typed failure outside it (plan §3.2).
- Heater (TP-state outlet): n_S3 = n_S2; T_S3 = 350 K specified; P_S3 = P_S2; Q_h = Ḣ(S3) − Ḣ(S2) computed, with S3's phase state (liquid or two-phase) determined by a TP flash at (350 K, P_r). Q_h may be negative.
- Flash (isothermal, isobaric, two outlets): n_S4 + n_S5 = n_S3; T_S4 = T_S5 = T_f; y_i = K_i(T_f, P) x_i for flowing phases; Q_f = Ḣ(S4) + Ḣ(S5) − Ḣ(S3) computed.
- Splitter: n_S6 = r n_S5, n_S7 = (1 − r) n_S5, same T, P, composition.

Because S6 is liquid at (T_f, P_r) with T_f and P known from the flash specification, the tear on S6 needs only its three component flows (plan §3.2). T01 must rediscover this from the incidence graph; it is not to be hard-coded.

### 4.1 Mixer outlet temperature is analytic

With equal c_p in both streams, both liquid, and both at P_r (so the v_i (P − P_r) term is zero; at any common P it is identical per mole and cancels anyway), the enthalpy closure is linear in T:

    T_S2 = (n_S1,tot · 300 K + n_S6,tot · T_f) / (n_S1,tot + n_S6,tot).

Nominal: T_S2 = (3·300 + 1.6391909·360)/4.6391909 = 321.200131081939 K. This closed form is a check on the K02 bracketed mixer solve, not a substitute for it.

## 5. Direct reference (oracle) derivation

Overall steady state of the loop: the recycle is S6 = r L x (liquid at T_f), so the flash feed is F + r L x, where F is the fresh-feed vector, L the flash liquid flow, x its composition. The flash component balance and equilibrium give, for each i,

    V y_i + L x_i = F_i + r L x_i,   y_i = K_i x_i   ⇒   x_i [V K_i + (1 − r) L] = F_i.

With q = V/L and a = 1 − r:

    x_i = F_i / (L (a + q K_i)),   y_i = K_i x_i,
    Σ x_i = 1 ⇒ L = Σ F_i/(a + q K_i),
    Σ y_i − Σ x_i = 0 ⇒ f(q) ≡ Σ (K_i − 1) F_i/(a + q K_i) = 0.

These are the plan §3.2 equations.

### 5.1 Reduction to the Rachford–Rice function of the fresh feed, and recycle invariance

Write a + q K_i = (a + q)[1 + β (K_i − 1)] with β ≡ q/(a + q). Then, with F_tot = Σ F_i and z_i = F_i/F_tot,

    f(q) = F_tot/(a + q) · RR(β),   RR(β) ≡ Σ z_i (K_i − 1)/(1 + β (K_i − 1)).

Since a + q > 0, f(q) = 0 ⇔ RR(β) = 0: the oracle root is the Rachford–Rice root of a **single TP flash of the fresh feed** at (T_f, P). Physically, β = q/(a + q) = V/(V + (1 − r)L) = V/(V + purge) = V/F_tot by the overall balance V + purge = F_tot, i.e. β is the fresh-feed vapor fraction. Furthermore L (a + q) = (1 − r) L + V = F_tot, so

    x_i = z_i / (1 + β (K_i − 1)),   y_i = K_i x_i,   V = β F_tot,   L = F_tot (1 − β)/(1 − r),   q = (1 − r) β/(1 − β).

This proves the plan §3.2 metamorphic check: V, x, y are independent of r; only L (hence recycle and q) scales as 1/(1 − r). The corollary that the SYN-001 tear map is benign (throughput scaling only, no composition–energy coupling) follows directly: the tear fixed point r L x has x independent of r. T06 must count the r-variants as one recycle case.

Uniqueness: RR is strictly decreasing on (1/(1 − K_max), 1/(1 − K_min)) ⊃ [0, 1]; RR(0) = Σ z_i K_i − 1 and RR(1) = 1 − Σ z_i/K_i. A root in (0, 1) exists and is unique iff Σ z_i K_i > 1 and Σ z_i/K_i > 1 (two-phase). If Σ z_i K_i ≤ 1 the feed is (sub-cooled or saturated) liquid; if Σ z_i/K_i ≤ 1 it is vapor. Both conditions cannot hold at once unless all K_i are equal to 1: by Cauchy–Schwarz (Σ z K)(Σ z/K) ≥ (Σ z)² = 1 with equality iff all K_i equal, so the oracle classification order (liquid test, then vapor test, else two-phase) is unambiguous on the SYN-001 domain, where the K_i are never all equal.

Zero components: a component with F_i = 0 has z_i = 0 and contributes exactly zero to RR, x_i = y_i = 0 exactly, and does not appear in K_max/K_min bracket selection (K of an absent component is irrelevant). The oracle must implement this exclusion (ADR 0001 D3.3).

## 6. Energy bookkeeping

Adiabatic mixer: Ḣ(S2) = Ḣ(S1) + Ḣ(S6). Splitter linearity: Ḣ(S5) = Ḣ(S6) + Ḣ(S7). Hence

    Q_h + Q_f = [Ḣ(S3) − Ḣ(S2)] + [Ḣ(S4) + Ḣ(S5) − Ḣ(S3)] = Ḣ(S4) + Ḣ(S7) − Ḣ(S1),

for every r: total duty equals external-product enthalpy minus fresh-feed enthalpy, and the internal recycle enthalpy cancels (plan §3.2). With the §2 enthalpies and the fresh feed at T_r (so Ḣ(S1) = 0 at P_r), the closed form is

    Q_h + Q_f = c_p (T_f − 300 K) F_tot + V Σ y_i L_i.

Nominal: 100·60·3 + 1.3608090692 × 28 173.03… = 56 338.069446743 W. The split for each variant is in §7. This check shares the SYN-001 thermodynamics with the solver and is labeled as such (blueprint A09): it verifies bookkeeping, not enthalpy data.

Per-variant duties are computed from the actual phase state of S3: when S3 is two-phase at 350 K, Ḣ(S3) uses the 350 K flash split of the mixed feed (vapor fraction β_h and compositions x_h, y_h in `reference_values.yaml`).

Findings recorded for downstream packages (none changes a scientific requirement):

1. **r = 0 is a phase-appearance case** (plan §3.2, confirmed): the equimolar feed is above its 347.44 K bubble point at 350 K. Registered as such, not treated as an accident.
2. **The 310 K and 420 K variants also have a two-phase heater outlet.** In the all-liquid variant the recycle has the feed composition (no vapor leaves), and in the all-vapor variant the recycle is zero, so in both the mixed feed is equimolar and the 350 K heater outlet is two-phase with β_h = 0.10136872. The plan lists these as single-phase *flash* cases; their heater outlet state is stated here so the K02 heater/flash TP kernel is tested with a two-phase heater outlet in three of the five variants.
3. **Negative heater duty at r = 0.95.** The adiabatic mixer outlet (354.73 K) is above the 350 K setpoint, so the "heater" removes 16 144.6 W. ADR 0001 D4.2 makes this a supported result. A heater implementation that asserts Q ≥ 0 would fail this registered variant.
4. **Exact zero-flow streams occur in three of five variants** (recycle at r = 0; vapor product at 310 K; liquid, purge, and recycle at 420 K). These exercise ADR 0001 D3 in the nominal fixture set, not only in adversarial cases.
5. **The v0.0 mixer domain restriction is never triggered by an r-variant.** The subcooling margin 1 − Σ z_mix K(T_mix) at T_f = 360 K is 0.767, 0.582, 0.187, 0.100, 0.0214, 0.00217, 0.000217 at r = 0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999, 0.9999 and tends to 0⁺ as r → 1 (T_mix → 360 K, z_mix → x). K02 needs a separate case (for example a fresh feed hotter than its bubble point) to test the typed mixer-domain failure.
6. **Recycle invariance holds exactly** in the oracle (§5.1) and is registered as the metamorphic check: V, x, y agree across r = 0, 0.5, 0.95 to the composition tolerance; L scales as 1/(1 − r). T06 counts the r-variants as one recycle case.
7. **The 420 K variant is r-independent** (recycle is zero for every r); the 310 K variant depends on r only through the recycle throughput L = 3/(1 − r).

Two further registered fixture inputs have expected *outcome types* rather than oracle values: a conflicting heater specification (outlet temperature and duty both fixed) must be rejected at validation as a structural over-specification (STR-03), and a deliberately capped solve budget must terminate with a typed budget-exhausted failure and no certificate.

## 8. Analytic linear recycle

t = f + r t with f = (1, 1, 1), solution t = f/(1 − r): t = (2, 2, 2) at r = 0.5 and (20, 20, 20) at r = 0.95. This isolates tear-solver behavior from the flash (plan §3.3; NUM-02).

## 9. Tolerances and oracle accuracy

Registered (plan §3.3, adopted in ADR 0001 D6) for SYN-001 only:

| Check | Absolute a_i | Relative r_i × scale s_i |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Component balance | 1e-9 mol/s | 1e-8 × 3 mol/s (registered throughput: fresh-feed total) |
| Energy balance | 1e-5 W | 1e-8 × 1e5 W (registered energy scale) |
| Temperature | 1e-6 K | — |
| Pressure | 1e-2 Pa | — |
| Normalized composition | 1e-10 | — |

Confirmation against oracle accuracy: the oracle solves RR(β) = 0 for a function whose derivative at the root is RR'(β*) = −Σ z_i (K_i − 1)²/(1 + β*(K_i − 1))² ≈ −0.56 at the nominal state (well away from zero), by bisection or a safeguarded Newton to machine precision on a bracket inside (1/(1 − K_max), 1/(1 − K_min)). Double-precision evaluation of K_i involves one exponential of an argument of magnitude ≈ 1, so the relative error of K_i and hence of β*, x, y, V, L is a few ulps (≲ 1e-15). The registered tolerances are therefore at least four orders of magnitude looser than oracle accuracy, and comparing the double-precision oracle to the 40-digit reference at 1e-13 relative is a meaningful test of the oracle. The tolerances are preimplementation synthetic-fixture choices and are not applied to real processes.

Scales registered for later ensemble generation (blueprint A04, T06): tear component flows scale 3 mol/s; temperatures 100 K; pressure 1e5 Pa; duties 1e5 W.

Registered initializer for the SYN-001 flowsheet tear (not a converged answer): **`SYN-001-tear-init-v2`, t⁰ = G(0)** — one sequential traversal from a dormant recycle (ADR 0001 D3.4 lets every unit accept a dormant inlet), i.e. r × the liquid of the TP flash of F at (T_f, P). By §5.1, G(0) = (1 − r) t* exactly: nominal (0.14888835696525697384, 0.27319848846280806123, 0.39750861996035914862) mol/s; r = 0.95 (0.28288787823398825029, 0.51907712807933531633, 0.75526637792468238237); (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) at 310 K; (0, 0, 0) at r = 0 and at 420 K. It is admissible at every variant: at 360 K it is saturated liquid of the flash's own composition, which the v0.0 mixer's intensive admissibility criterion admits (decision register R-007). The earlier registered guess recycle_i = r·F_i (`SYN-001-tear-init-v1`, P01) is **retired** (2026-09-21, register R-014): it names an equimolar stream at the flash temperature, which lies outside the v0.0 mixer's subcooled-liquid domain at three of the five variants (Σ z_i K_i = 1.3837 at 360 K for every r > 0; 5.068 at 420 K). It survives only as the guess of the adversarial case `SYN-001-inadmissible-guess`, which exists to exercise the initializer-rejection path of blueprint §7.4. The NUM-02 initializer t_i = f_i (§8) is unaffected: that recycle has no mixer.

Two cautions for anyone using G(0) as solver evidence. The tear map is exactly affine along the ray through t* — R(s t*) = (1 − r)(1 − s) t*, measured by K02 to 1.1e-14 and derived from the fact that adding saturated liquid of the flash's own composition to a two-phase mixture at the same T and P changes only L — so a Newton started at G(0) reaches t* in one step and exercises no globalization; and at 310 K and 420 K the map is affine on the whole domain (pure A is liquid at 310 K, pure C is vapour at 420 K). The registered variants therefore test the initializer, the exact tear derivative and the convergence test; the off-ray starts that test the damped Newton and the phase restart are registered in `docs/derivations/K03-solver-spec.md` §13.

## 10. What this derivation does and does not establish

- Establishes: internal thermodynamic consistency of SYN-001 (h from g; K from μ equality; boiling points exact at P_r); the algebraic reference for every registered variant; recycle invariance; energy closure; phase state of every registered stream.
- Does not establish: any empirical validity (synthetic model), any simulator benchmark result, or correctness of the production flash/recycle solver (K02/K03), which must be compared to the oracle independently. The oracle is implemented separately from the production solver (`benchmarks/syn001/oracle.py`, no imports from `process_runtime`).
